gate: Relational Locality / Sparse Source Closure Gate

generic_path_counterexample.target: edge (1,2) BKM metrics + polar transport response
generic_path_counterexample.theorem: No exact bounded-neighborhood state descriptor built only from proper-subsystem marginals can determine generic local ETL/QMAR response, because the hidden full-body completion can change the response while every proper marginal agrees.

prior_exchange_locality_boundary.result: v12.49 already proved that sparse connected exchange incidence alone saturates the complete exchange algebra; paths/cycles/stars do not reduce the exact solder module.
prior_exchange_locality_boundary.relation: v13.15 is stronger/different for QMAR: even a site-local source on a tree can have a local geometric response that depends on hidden global completion data.

commuting_markov_positive_sector.state_class: strictly positive commuting Gibbs/Markov network with log rho equal to a sum of mutually commuting clique potentials
commuting_markov_positive_sector.source_class: ETL/PGRL source P contained in the same commuting clique algebra
commuting_markov_positive_sector.closure_theorem: log rho_s = log rho + sP - log Z_s remains in the same graphical exponential family exactly; junction-tree messages are an exact sufficient state for local marginals and their source derivatives.
commuting_markov_positive_sector.binary_complexity: message state per separator O(2^w); exact inference O(N 2^(w+1)) for treewidth w

noncommuting_source_boundary.result: A local source outside the commuting clique algebra immediately leaves the classical/commuting Markov representation, so separator-message closure is not generic ETL closure.

next_gate.name: Quantum Markov / Conditional-Mutual-Information Selection Gate
next_gate.question: Can the retained global-consistency/provenance ontology force or naturally select the commuting/quantum-Markov condition needed for separator closure? Test conditional mutual information across graph separators, Petz recoverability, and source stability. If exact Markovity is not selected, quantify whether an ontology-native recoverability bound can provide a certified approximate locality theorem without introducing heuristics.
